newsitem.title: FRANCE: For new French political party, it's a dog's life.
newsitem.headline: For new French political party, it's a dog's life.

text.p: Dogs, cats and other pets should have birth and death certificates just like their owners, a new French political party said on Thursday.
The party's campaign aims to foster "new relationships between mankind, animals and nature".

Setting out its platform, the Movement for Mankind, Animals and Nature said all pets should be given mandatory tattoos for identification purposes and be registered at town halls so the state can keep track of them should they change address, run away, get a new owner or die.

The new party also called for low-cost public clinics so that people who are homeless or out of work can afford medical care for their pets, and for easier access to public spaces so that Rover -- or Medor, as he would be known in France -- can better enjoy his town's gardens and parks along with his owner.
But the movement also said it favours eating farm animals -- as long as they are not confined to tiny cages or trucked more than eight hours en route to the slaughterhouse.
